summary: Implement security hardening for v1.0 without changing UI or existing functionality. The changes include: (1) Extend the data‑reset flow to delete the encryption key from SecureStore and preserve the policy‑acceptance flag. (2) Ensure encrypted‑backup temporary files are always removed after the share sheet finishes (success, cancellation or error). (3) Enforce a minimum 12‑character backup passphrase, display the rule before typing, validate live as the user types and on submission, and show the error under the input field. (4) Update backup/restore logic to read receipt photo bytes via the new expo‑file‑system `File` API (`new File(uri).bytes()`) and to write them back with `File.write`, updating each receipt’s `photoUri` after restore. (5) Add numeric validation utilities for receipt amount, mileage miles, mileage rate and tax rate with user‑friendly helper‑text errors, and integrate them into the corresponding entry and settings screens. (6) Add a strict backup format validator that checks version number and the shape/types of receipt and mileage arrays before any data mutation during restore; on failure a friendly error is shown and no data is altered. (7) Disable CSV and PDF export buttons while an export is in progress to prevent concurrent exports. (8) Add unit tests for the new behaviours: encryption‑key purge on data reset, backup passphrase rule, numeric field validation, and backup‑format validation before restore. All changes keep existing screens, labels, flows, look‑and‑feel, and existing tests intact.
steps: 1️⃣ Add a new module `src/lib/validation.ts` that exports pure validation functions: `validateReceiptAmount`, `validateMileageMiles`, `validateMileageRate`, `validateTaxRate`, and `validateBackupPassphrase`. Each returns `null` when valid or an error string for UI consumption.

2️⃣ Update UI screens that accept numeric input – `ReceiptEntryScreen.tsx`, `MileageEntryScreen.tsx`, and `TaxSettingsScreen.tsx` – to import the validation helpers, call them on each change, store the error messages in state, display a `<HelperText type="error">` under the field, and disable the Save button until all fields are valid.

3️⃣ In `BackupPassphraseScreen.tsx` import `validateBackupPassphrase`, enforce a minimum length of 12 characters, render the rule text above the input, run live validation as the user types, and show an error under the field. Adjust the Create Backup button to be disabled when the rule is not satisfied.

4️⃣ Create/extend `src/lib/files.ts` (or edit the existing one) to provide two async helpers: `readFileBytes(uri: string): Promise<Uint8Array>` using `new File(uri).bytes()` and `writeFileBytes(uri: string, data: Uint8Array): Promise<void>` using `File.write(uri, data)`. Export them for use in backup logic.

5️⃣ Refactor `src/lib/backup.ts` –
   • When creating a backup, after `Sharing.shareAsync(tempUri)` resolves (or rejects) delete the temporary file with `FileSystem.deleteAsync(tempUri, { idempotent: true })` inside a `finally` block.
   • Replace any legacy `readAsStringAsync`/`writeAsStringAsync` calls for receipt photos with the new `readFileBytes` / `writeFileBytes` helpers, base‑64‑encode the bytes for inclusion in the backup JSON.
   • Add a new pure function `validateBackupStructure(data: any): string | null` that checks `data.version` is the expected constant and that `data.receipts` and `data.mileage` are arrays whose objects contain the required fields with correct types (e.g., amount: number, date: string, etc.).
   • In `restoreBackup`, after decrypting, call `validateBackupStructure`. If it returns an error, throw an `Error` with a friendly message; otherwise proceed with the existing restore routine.

6️⃣ Modify `src/lib/dataReset.ts` – after invoking the store’s `clearAll()` (which wipes receipts,mileage, etc.), delete the stored encryption key using `SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(KEY_NAME)` (the same key used by the native storage provider). Preserve the policy acceptance by reading it before the clear, then writing it back after the key is regenerated (or by ensuring the policy flag lives outside the encrypted KV store).

7️⃣ In `src/screens/ExportScreen.tsx` (or the `ExportButton` component) introduce a boolean state `exportRunning`. When a CSV or PDF export starts, set the flag, disable both export buttons, and reset the flag when the async export completes (including error paths). The buttons’ `disabled` prop will now reflect this state.

8️⃣ Add unit tests:
   • `__tests__/dataReset.test.ts` – mock `expo-secure-store` and verify that calling the data‑reset function deletes the encryption key and that the policy‑accepted flag remains true.
   • `__tests__/passphraseRules.test.ts` – import `validateBackupPassphrase` and confirm it rejects strings shorter than 12 characters and accepts a valid 12‑plus‑character passphrase.
   • `__tests__/validation.test.ts` – import the numeric validation helpers and test boundary conditions (e.g., amount ≤ 0, amount > 1 000 000, more than two decimals, mileage > 10 000, rate outside 0‑5, tax > 100). Ensure the correct error messages are returned.
   • `__tests__/restoreValidation.test.ts` – create a mock store with some data, craft a malformed backup JSON (missing fields or wrong types), call `restoreBackup` and assert it throws, and also assert that the store’s data is unchanged after the failed restore.
   All tests should use the in‑memory store (`createStore(createMemoryRawStore(), createMemoryKeyProvider())`) and run under Jest as other unit tests do.
9️⃣ Run the full test suite (`npm test`) and the TypeScript compiler (`npx tsc --noEmit`) to ensure no regressions. Adjust any type errors caused by the new imports or API changes.
🔟 Verify that the UI still matches the design tokens (no visual changes) and that the existing acceptance tests continue to pass.
